scope: Real, measured timings from a single run (process.hrtime.bigint() around each phase, process.memoryUsage().heapUsed sampled immediately before/after) — not estimated, not averaged across multiple runs. Compares adapter-mediated access against a direct-canonical-access baseline for the same 3,697 entities.

measurements.directCanonicalAccessNote: Baseline: reading entity.origin.country for all 3,697 entities directly, no adapter involved.
measurements.fullCollectionAdapterNote: lib/adapters/legacy-datasets.js's buildLegacyDatasets() — produces all 5 legacy collections (names, namesEnriched, popularity, categories, variants) from the same 3,697 entities.

interpretation: The full adapter pass (producing all 5 legacy collections) takes ~23.6ms for the entire 3,697-name catalog — roughly 59x slower than direct field access, but still two orders of magnitude below any page-generation timescale that would matter in a build pipeline (audit/canonical-performance.json, Phase 3A, measured the underlying canonical build itself at ~90ms for the same 3,697 entities).

Memory overhead (~2.9 MB for the full adapter output) is a one-time cost to materialize 5 flat collections in memory simultaneously; a generator that only needs one collection (e.g. just `names`) would see a smaller footprint than this combined figure.

This measurement is intentionally informational only, per the Phase 3B brief — no generator currently reads through the adapter, so there is no real production workload to benchmark against yet. These numbers establish a baseline for a future phase that would.
